text:
Mikael Backlund is 37 and has played more than 1,100 NHL games, all for Calgary, and his season line looks like an old player's: 7 points in 21 games, none on the power play. The truth is kinder than that.

Calgary has scored 9 fewer goals than expected with Backlund on the ice, and he has 3 goals on 5.6 expected (the quality of his chances), shooting 5.6% against a league norm of 13.3%. Our numbers flag him as due. His ice time has gone up, to 19.2 minutes over his last ten, which says the Flames still trust him.

His value has long been the stuff that doesn't show in points. Evolving-Hockey had him at replacement level overall last season but in the 88th percentile for taking chances away, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 97th percentile among forwards for primary shot assists. He scored the Flames' only goal in a blowout loss in Anaheim, a top-shelf finish. A few more of those and the line will look like him again.
headline: Backlund's numbers are worse than his game
